response: Reimplantation of spinal cord arteries during thoracic and thoracoabdominal aneurysm repair is not necessary. With the use of monitoring techniques such as motor evoked potentials (MEP) and somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEP), it is possible to safely sacrifice multiple intercostal and lumbar arteries without reimplantation, resulting in low rates of paraplegia. This suggests that routine reimplantation of spinal cord arteries is not indicated, and advancements in understanding spinal cord perfusion may eventually allow for endovascular repair of the entire thoracic aorta without spinal cord injury.
